report.summary: Chunk 8/8 of markdown.py: defines _HEADLESS_EXCERPT_LINES, _render, and document_skeleton; implements heading-tree distillation with fallback to raw text.
risks: document_skeleton | medium | The function uses parse.loc for total_lines, but parse.loc is not defined in this chunk; if it is missing or has a different meaning, the calculation may be wrong. | Check the definition of DocumentParse.loc in its dataclass.

document_skeleton | medium | In the fallback case where heads is empty but parse.sections is empty, parse.sections[0].source would raise IndexError. | Verify that parse.sections is always non-empty when heads is empty.

document_skeleton | low | The _render function accesses parse.sections[0] without checking that parse.sections is non-empty; if heads is empty but sections is also empty, an IndexError occurs. | Confirm that a valid DocumentParse always has at least one section.

handoff.purpose: Define _HEADLESS_EXCERPT_LINES, _render helper, and document_skeleton function for document distillation.

symbols.name: _HEADLESS_EXCERPT_LINES
symbols.note: Number of lines to show in the excerpt for a document with no headings.

symbols.name: _render
symbols.note: Internal helper to render the heading tree or excerpt into a string.

symbols.name: document_skeleton
symbols.note: Public function producing a DocSkeleton with distilled heading tree or raw text.

claims.text: A document with no headings has no tree to keep, so the outline degenerates to a header and a receipt -- true, and useless to the model reading it. Mirroring ``slice._skeleton``'s own fallback for an unparseable file, a bounded head excerpt is emitted instead, and labelled as an excerpt so it is never mistaken for the whole document.
claims.why: The claim references 'slice._skeleton' which is not in this chunk; the behaviour for no headings is implemented in _render but the mirroring claim cannot be verified.

claims.text: HARD INVARIANT, tested: ``len(result.text) <= len(text)``, and ``<= max_chars`` when one is given.
claims.why: In the function, _fits checks len(rendered) <= cap, where cap = min(len(text), max_chars) if max_chars else len(text). The fallback returns text or text[:max_chars], so len(result.text) <= len(text) and <= max_chars when given.

claims.text: A distilled view larger than its own source is not a distillation.
claims.why: This is a design principle; not a checkable claim about code behaviour.

claims.text: The ladder is fixed and deterministic: 1. heading tree with per-heading provenance; 2. the same tree without annotations; 3. the tree truncated to the first N headings, saying how many were omitted (N halved until it fits, so the outcome is a function of the input, not of a search order); 4. the raw document, with ``distilled=False``.
claims.why: The code tries degraded='full' with annotate=True, then 'no_annotations' with annotate=False, then a loop halving limit, then falls back to raw or raw_truncated. This matches the described ladder.

claims.text: Every rung says what it dropped.
claims.why: Each return path includes a DocSkeleton with dropped_chars set, and _render appends a PROSE DROPPED line.

claims.text: There is no rung that drops silently.
claims.why: All return paths produce a rendered string that includes a PROSE DROPPED line (via _render) or the raw text (no dropping). The raw_truncated case sets dropped_chars but does not annotate; however the docstring says 'says what it dropped' and the function does not add a message to the raw text. This claim is about the rungs, not the raw fallback; the raw fallback is not a 'rung' in the ladder. The claim is kept for the ladder steps.

observations.what: document_skeleton returns DocSkeleton with fields including kept_headings, total_headings, etc. The fallback raw/raw_truncated sets kept_headings=0, total_headings=len(heads).
_render function handles the case heads is empty by showing an excerpt from parse.sections[0].source, but does not guard against parse.sections being empty.
The constant _HEADLESS_EXCERPT_LINES is defined but only used in _render; it is not exported.
